result.title: StructRL: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning with Replay Graphs
result.summary: StructRL turns the experience collected during reinforcement learning into an explicit replay graph. Once the graph contains a path to the task goal, dynamic programming selects actions on the observed part of the state space; these actions form a graph policy that is defined only where the required transitions have been observed. StructRL transfers these actions to model-free learners: as action preferences for a DQN Q-model and as target directions along shortest observed paths for a SAC actor. For DQN on three sparse-reward MiniGrid tasks, final success rises from 0.10 to 0.90 (DoorKey), 0.10 to 0.80 (KeyCorridor) and 0 to 0.50 (ObstructedMaze); plain DQN does not catch up with three times the budget. For SAC on continuous PointMaze, graph-derived direction labels raise final success from 0.17 to 1.0 on seven matched runs that reached the goal. Distilling the graph policy into a fresh Q-model gives a DoorKey 6x6 controller that reaches the goal from 91% of reachable states, against 38% for plain DQN. Scaling experiments identify three bottlenecks: incomplete graph support, structural aliasing, and loss of graph information in high-dimensional inputs.

AI.brief_summary: StructRL 将强化学习过程中收集的经验组织成显式 replay graph，在已观测状态上通过动态规划求取通向目标的动作，并把图策略以动作偏好或最短路径方向标签的形式蒸馏给 DQN、SAC 等 model-free 学习器，在稀疏奖励 MiniGrid 与连续 PointMaze 上显著提升成功率，同时分析了图覆盖不全、结构别名和高维输入下图信息丢失三个瓶颈。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉语言推理工作，但其将结构化图策略蒸馏进策略网络、并把「结构别名」与「高维输入中图信息丢失」作为失败原因，可供核查 latent 状态是否保留任务必要信息及监督信号如何注入表示的线索。
